title: Pentesting Vendors With 48-Hour Delivery in 2026: Who Delivers What
summary: Which pentest vendors deliver in 48 hours? A dated 2026 comparison of CodeAnt AI, Intruder, Aikido, Cobalt, Astra, BreachLock, Synack and XBOW.
body_markdown:
CodeAnt AI delivers a full penetration test report within 48 hours, with findings proven exploitable and every critical finding checked by a security researcher before it reaches you. It fits security and engineering leads with a SOC 2 audit, an enterprise customer review or a release date coming up, who need black, grey or white box testing across web apps, APIs and cloud.


Intruder, Aikido, Cobalt's Autonomous Pentest and Astra's Pentest Auto also publish same-day or 24-hour turnarounds, mostly for narrower scopes such as a single web app. BreachLock's human-led PTaaS can launch in 24 to 48 hours but then tests for days to weeks, and Synack's assessment windows run 4 to 5 business days or longer.


CodeAnt AI has run 12,000 pentests and is trusted by more than 1,000 companies, including Fortune 500 companies like NRG, cybersecurity leaders like Commvault, and fast-growing companies like 11x and Sanas.


This guide compares eight vendors that publish fast turnarounds, using each vendor's own pages (checked November 4, 2026), explains what starts the clock, and lists the questions that separate a real 48-hour pentest from fast output.

## What Does 48-Hour Pentest Delivery Actually Means?


48-hour delivery does not always mean the same thing across vendors.


In some cases, it means the vendor can start testing within 48 hours. In other cases, it means initial findings are delivered within 48 hours. Some vendors use it to describe a complete report turnaround for a narrow scope.


Before choosing a provider, clarify which version they mean.


A real 48-hour pentest delivery model should define:


-


Time to kickoff


-


Time to first validated finding


-


Time to critical alert


-


Time to full report


-


Time to retest after remediation


-


Time to final evidence package


For a security team, these timelines matter differently.


A critical vulnerability should not wait for the final report. If a vendor confirms an authentication bypass, exposed customer data, or cloud credential leak, the team should receive immediate notification.


The full[report](https://codeant.ai/pentest-sample-report) can follow.


This is the difference between fast communication and rushed reporting.


### The four clocks vendors quote


When a vendor quotes a time, ask which of these four clocks it is.

CodeAnt AI: within 48 hours; Cobalt Autonomous Pentest: 24 hours

Only the last clock ends your deadline. If a vendor's quoted time is the first or second clock, add the testing window and the report on top.


## When Does the 48-Hour Clock Start, and What Happens Inside It?


The clock starts when the scope is agreed and the tester has the access the test needs. What that access is depends on the type of test:


-


Black box: only your root domain. The tester finds your subdomains, IP addresses and exposed services the way an attacker would, so there is nothing to set up.


-


Grey box: working test accounts as well, ideally at the lowest privilege level, so the tester can check whether one user or tenant can see or change another's data. If your login needs MFA or SSO, sort out how the tester gets past it before the start date. A login step the tester cannot pass delays the start.


-


White box: code repository or cloud access as well, so findings can be traced back to the code that caused them.


NIST's guide to security testing (SP 800-115) splits a penetration test into four phases: planning, discovery, attack and reporting, with reporting running alongside the other three. In a 48-hour AI pentest at CodeAnt AI, those phases look like this:


1.


Planning: scope and rules of engagement are confirmed, and access is checked.


2.


Discovery: the attack surface is mapped, including domains, subdomains, IP addresses, open ports, hosting providers and third-party services, to find what is reachable from outside.


3.


Attack: AI agents attack the reachable surface for several hours and chain issues into attack paths. Security researchers then take the agents' results, try to go further, and check every critical finding before it goes into the report.


4.


Reporting: you receive an executive summary you can share with auditors and customers, and a detailed section for engineers with each finding's severity score, the evidence of what was reached and the steps to reproduce it.


After the report, the calendar is mostly yours. Your team fixes the findings, CodeAnt AI re-scans after each fix at no charge, and the updated report shows which issues are closed. Teams that fix quickly can have a re-verified report within days of the first one.


## When A 48-Hour Pentest Makes Sense


A rapid pentest is not always the right model. Some systems need deeper testing over a longer period.


But 48-hour pentesting can be very useful in specific situations.


### Customer security review is blocking a deal


Enterprise buyers often ask for recent pentest evidence before signing.


If the company does not have a recent report, a 48-hour pentest can help unblock procurement. But the report must include credible scope, methodology, findings, remediation status, and retest plans.


### SOC 2 evidence is urgently needed


A SaaS team preparing for SOC 2 may need to show that penetration testing was performed and that findings were addressed.


A fast pentest can support the audit, especially when paired with proof-of-exploit and retesting evidence.


### A major release needs security validation


If a new authentication flow, billing workflow, API gateway, or cloud deployment is going live, a rapid test can validate the highest-risk areas before or immediately after launch.


### A new external asset was exposed


If a staging app, admin panel, storage bucket, API, or cloud service becomes public, fast testing can determine whether the exposure creates real risk.


### A fix needs retest confirmation


Sometimes the urgent need is not initial testing. It is verification.


A 48-hour retest SLA may be more valuable than a 48-hour first report because unresolved findings often block audits and customer approvals.


## What A Fast Pentest Should Include


A fast pentest should not mean a thin pentest.


Even under a compressed timeline, the vendor should provide evidence that the testing was meaningful.


### Clear scope


The vendor should define what was tested.


This may include:


-


Web application


-


APIs


-


Authentication flows


-


Cloud assets


-


External attack surface


-


Specific release changes


-


Admin workflows


-


Tenant boundaries


-


CI/CD exposure


A vague scope weakens the value of the report.


### Reconnaissance


Even a 48-hour pentest should include reconnaissance.


For external testing, this may involve:


-


Subdomain discovery


-


Certificate Transparency review


-


Public port exposure


-


API endpoint discovery


-


JavaScript bundle analysis


-


Public cloud asset discovery


-


Technology fingerprinting


Reconnaissance helps testers understand what an attacker can see from outside.


### Exploit validation


This is the most important part.


The vendor should confirm whether findings are exploitable.


A useful finding should include:


-


Affected endpoint


-


Request method


-


User role used


-


Payload or test condition


-


Response evidence


-


Business impact


-


Severity explanation


-


Remediation guidance


Without exploit validation, the report may be closer to a scan than a pentest.


### Prioritized reporting


Fast pentest reports should not bury security teams in noise.


They should clearly separate:


-


Critical findings


-


High findings


-


Medium findings


-


Low findings


-


Informational observations


-


Retest requirements


A fast report is useful only when the team knows what to fix first.


### Retesting path


The vendor should explain how fixes will be verified.


A finding is not fully closed until remediation is tested.


## What A 48-Hour Pentest Should Not Be


A 48-hour pentest should not be a rebranded scanner export.


Scanner reports can be useful, but they are not the same as penetration testing.


Watch out for vendors that only provide:


-


Long CVE lists without proof


-


Generic severity scores


-


No affected user role


-


No reproduction steps


-


No business impact


-


No retesting workflow


-


No explanation of exploitability


-


No evidence safe enough for auditors


If the vendor cannot prove what was exploitable, the report may not satisfy engineering, customers, or compliance teams.


Fast does not mean shallow.


Fast should mean focused.

## What SLAs Matter More Than The 48-Hour Claim


The phrase “48-hour delivery” sounds simple, but buyers should ask for specific SLAs.


### Critical finding notification SLA


If a critical issue is found, the vendor should notify you immediately.


Not at the end of the report cycle.


### Report delivery SLA


This defines when you receive the written report.


Make sure it includes validated findings, not only automated output.


### Retest SLA


This is one of the most important SLAs.


Ask how quickly the vendor will verify fixes after your team deploys remediation.


### Evidence delivery SLA


For SOC 2 or customer reviews, ask when the final evidence package will be available.


This may include:


-


Final report


-


Retest report


-


Finding status


-


Screenshots or request evidence


-


Severity rationale


-


Scope and methodology


### Support response SLA


If engineering has questions about remediation, the vendor should be available quickly.


A report without responsive support slows down fixing.

## Is a 48-Hour Pentest Deep Enough, And Will My Auditor Accept It?


Depth comes from what gets tested and proven, not from calendar days. A 48-hour AI pentest shortens the waiting, not the testing: the agents work the attack surface continuously, and the researchers spend their time on validation and on the attack paths the agents could not finish.


Speed is not what an auditor checks. For SOC 2 and ISO 27001, the questions are whether an independent third party ran the test, whether the scope covered the systems in the audit, what was found, and whether you fixed it. Agree the scope with your auditor before the test, especially if your product has logins and tenants, where a grey box test shows far more than an external one.


Vendors handle the auditor question differently. Intruder refunds the test if an auditor rejects its report. Aikido's own page notes that some standards and auditors still require a pentest performed by a human. CodeAnt AI has a security researcher check every critical finding before it reaches you, and delivers a SOC 2 and ISO 27001-ready report with an executive summary written for auditors and customers.

## How Do You Check a Vendor's 48-Hour Claim?


Use this checklist before choosing a provider.


-


What starts the 48-hour clock: the signed order, payment, or confirmed access?


-


Which part of the report can I share with my auditor and my customers, and which part is for engineers only?


-


Does 48-hour delivery mean kickoff, first finding, or full report?


-


Is exploit validation included?


-


Are critical findings reported immediately?


-


Is authenticated testing included?


-


Are APIs tested?


-


Is cloud exposure tested?


-


Are CI/CD secrets or leaked credentials checked?


-


Is retesting included?


-


Is a formal retest report provided?


-


Is evidence safe for SOC 2 or customer reviews?


-


Are findings mapped to business impact?


-


Does the vendor provide remediation guidance?


-


Does the vendor offer support after the report?


If the vendor cannot answer these clearly, the 48-hour claim may not mean much.

A full enterprise assessment across multiple products, cloud accounts, internal networks, mobile apps, and complex business workflows may need more time.

-

-

-

-

-

-

-

The best vendors will tell you when 48 hours is appropriate and when it is not.
